questions.question_text: When the RBI wants to reduce the money supply in the economy to control inflation, it is most likely to:
options: Lower the repo rate and the cash reserve ratio
Reduce the bank rate and buy government securities
Raise the repo rate and the cash reserve ratio
Lower the statutory liquidity ratio and buy securities

questions.question_text: The rate at which the RBI lends short-term funds to commercial banks against government securities is the:
options: Bank rate
Reverse repo rate
Repo rate
Marginal cost lending rate

questions.question_text: The rate at which the RBI absorbs the surplus liquidity from banks is the:
options: Repo rate
Base rate
Prime lending rate
Reverse repo rate

questions.question_text: A bank has net demand and time liabilities (NDTL) of Rs 500 crore and the CRR is 4%. The cash it must keep with the RBI is:
options: Rs 125 crore
Rs 2 crore
Rs 4 crore
Rs 20 crore

questions.question_text: With an NDTL of Rs 500 crore and an SLR of 18%, the bank must hold liquid assets of:
options: Rs 90 crore
Rs 18 crore
Rs 180 crore
Rs 9 crore

questions.question_text: The main difference between CRR and SLR is that CRR is kept:
options: With the bank itself, while SLR is kept in cash with the RBI
In gold, while SLR is kept in cash
In cash with the RBI, while SLR is held in liquid assets with the bank itself
In shares, while SLR is kept in deposits

questions.question_text: Which of these is NOT eligible to be counted towards the SLR?
options: Cash in hand with the bank
Government approved securities
Equity shares of listed companies
Gold held by the bank

questions.question_text: The RBI is called the "banker's bank" because it:
options: Holds the reserves of banks and acts as their lender of last resort
Collects the income tax on behalf of the banks and the government
Gives loans and opens savings accounts for individual citizens
Sells shares of the commercial banks to the public at large

questions.question_text: The RBI acts as the "lender of last resort" when:
options: Commercial banks cannot obtain funds from any other source in a crisis
Individuals need housing loans for a long period of time
The government wants to borrow money from foreign banks and funds
Companies need long-term finance for expanding their plants

questions.question_text: The sole authority to issue currency notes of the denomination of Rs 2 and above in India is the:
options: State Bank of India
Mint at Nashik
Ministry of Finance
Reserve Bank of India
questions.explanation: Currency issue (Rs 1 is by the Ministry of Finance).

questions.question_text: The Re 1 note and the coins are issued by the:
options: National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development
Ministry of Finance, Government of India
State Bank of India
Reserve Bank of India
questions.explanation: Exception to the RBI's note issue.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a primary function of a commercial bank?
options: Fixing the bank rate
Issuing currency notes
Accepting deposits and granting loans
Controlling the credit in the economy

questions.question_text: A commercial bank creates credit by:
options: Lending out of deposits, which come back as fresh deposits
Printing notes on its own whenever the customers want loans
Selling foreign exchange to the customers who want to travel
Lending only its own capital and not the deposits of customers

questions.question_text: If the CRR is 10% and the initial deposit is Rs 1,000, the maximum total deposit creation is (money multiplier = 1/CRR):
options: Rs 100

questions.question_text: The money multiplier is 5 and the initial deposit is Rs 2,00,000. The total deposits created are:
The money multiplier of 5 corresponds to a reserve ratio of:
A savings deposit is mainly characterised by:
options: Easy withdrawal, low interest and no fixed tenure
No interest at all and no facility for withdrawals
Withdrawal only on the maturity of the deposit
Fixed tenure with a higher rate of interest on the deposit

questions.question_text: A current account is mostly meant for:
options: Senior citizens who want regular income
Students who want to save
Businessmen who make many transactions daily
Salaried persons who want a high interest
questions.explanation: No interest, no limits on transactions.

questions.question_text: A fixed deposit differs from a recurring deposit in that:
options: Both are repayable on demand
A lump sum is deposited once in a fixed deposit, while a recurring deposit takes monthly instalments
A recurring deposit takes a lump sum while a fixed deposit takes monthly instalments
Both take monthly instalments

questions.question_text: The interest on a fixed deposit of Rs 1,00,000 at 7% p.a. for one year (simple, ignoring the compounding) is:
options: Rs 700

questions.question_text: Premature withdrawal of a fixed deposit usually results in:
options: A bonus from the bank
No change in the interest
A higher rate of interest
A penalty or a lower rate of interest

questions.question_text: A recurring deposit of Rs 1,000 a month for 12 months with no interest has a maturity value of:
A cheque with two parallel lines across its face is a:
options: Stale cheque, which is not valid for payment
Order cheque, payable in cash over the counter
Crossed cheque, payable only through a bank account
Bearer cheque, payable to anyone who presents it

questions.question_text: A cheque is treated as stale if presented after:
options: One year from the date of its issue
One month from the date of its issue
Six months from the date of its issue
Three months from the date of its issue

questions.question_text: A post-dated cheque is one that:
options: Bears a date later than the date on which it is issued
Has no date
Is cancelled
Bears a date earlier than the date of issue

questions.question_text: Dishonour of a cheque for insufficient funds is an offence under:
options: Section 420 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860
Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act
The Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934
The Banking Regulation Act, 1949

questions.question_text: "Endorsement" of a cheque means:
options: Signing on its back to transfer it to another person
Drawing two parallel lines across the face of the cheque
Writing the amount in figures on the front of the cheque
Instructing the bank to stop the payment of the cheque

questions.question_text: A bearer cheque is payable to:
options: Only the person named as payee on the cheque
Whoever presents it at the counter of the bank
Only the person to whom it is endorsed on its back
Only the account holder who issued the cheque

questions.question_text: The drawer of a cheque is the:
options: Person to whom it is payable
Bank on which it is drawn
Person who issues the cheque
Person who endorses it

questions.question_text: The drawee of a cheque is the:
options: Person who issues it
Bank on which the cheque is drawn
Person who receives it
Person who crosses it

questions.question_text: The payee of a cheque is the:
options: Person to whom the amount is payable
Person who endorses it
Bank which pays it
Person who signs it

questions.question_text: NEFT settlements take place:
options: In batches at half-hourly intervals, round the clock
In real time for each transaction individually
Once a day
Once a week

questions.question_text: RTGS is meant for:
options: Cash deposits made over the counter of a branch
Large-value transfers, settled in real time one by one
Foreign remittances made through the authorised dealers
Small-value transfers of up to Rs 50,000 settled in batches

questions.question_text: The minimum value for an RTGS transaction is:
options: Rs 5 lakh
Rs 1 lakh
Rs 2 lakh

questions.question_text: IMPS allows:
options: Transfers only during the working hours of the bank
Transfers only through the cheques and demand drafts
Instant interbank transfers round the clock, even on holidays
Transfers only for a value above Rs 2 lakh

questions.question_text: Which one is the most suitable for sending Rs 5 crore to a supplier on the same day?
options: Demand draft
RTGS
NEFT
Money order

questions.question_text: A demand draft is:
options: A prepaid instrument issued by a bank, payable on demand
A cheque issued by a customer on his own account
A slip printed by an ATM after a cash withdrawal
A receipt issued for a cash deposit made by a customer

questions.question_text: A banker's cheque (pay order) is issued by:
options: A bank against payment made by the customer
The customer from his own account with the bank
The post office against a deposit by a customer
The RBI on behalf of the commercial banks

questions.question_text: Core banking solution (CBS) allows a customer to:
options: Use only the ATMs
Operate the account only from the home branch
Operate the account from any branch of the bank
Withdraw only the cash

questions.question_text: An ATM allows a customer to:
options: Open fixed deposits and recurring deposits only
Take loans without any documents or any security at all
Pay only the taxes due to the government and nothing else
Withdraw cash, check the balance and do some transactions any time

questions.question_text: A debit card differs from a credit card in that a debit card:
options: Gives unlimited credit
Needs no PIN
Gives a loan with an interest-free period
Deducts money directly from the account balance

questions.question_text: A credit card allows its holder to:
options: Pay no interest ever
Withdraw money without repaying
Borrow within a limit and repay later
Spend only the money in the account

questions.question_text: A prepaid card:
options: Is valid for withdrawals from the ATM machines only
Is loaded with a fixed amount in advance and used until it is spent
Is linked to a loan taken by the holder from the bank
Is linked to a credit limit that is fixed by the bank

questions.question_text: Mobile banking apps typically require authentication through:
options: A visit to the branch
Login credentials, an OTP or biometrics
A signed letter
The photocopy of the passbook

questions.question_text: Which one is NOT a function of a commercial bank?
options: Issuing currency notes
Agency services such as collecting cheques
Accepting deposits
Granting loans

questions.question_text: "Agency functions" of a bank include:
options: Printing the currency notes for the whole country
Setting the interest rates for the whole country
Collecting cheques and paying premiums on behalf of customers
Controlling the foreign exchange of the whole country

questions.question_text: Priority sector lending includes loans for:
options: Gold imports by the jewellers
Speculative trading on the stock market
Luxury goods imported from abroad
Agriculture, MSMEs, education and housing

questions.question_text: NABARD is the apex institution for:
options: Housing finance for the urban households
Foreign trade and export credit
Industrial finance for the large industries
Agriculture and rural development

questions.question_text: SIDBI is the principal institution for:
options: Housing finance for the urban middle class
Promotion and financing of small-scale industries
Export and import finance for large companies
Agriculture and the allied activities in villages

questions.question_text: The Exim Bank of India deals mainly with:
options: Financing of exports and imports
Rural credit through cooperative banks
Education loans for the students
Housing finance for the individual borrowers

questions.question_text: The National Housing Bank is a:
options: Life insurance company in the public sector
Commercial bank that accepts demand deposits
Regulator and promoter of housing finance companies
Cooperative bank at the state level

questions.question_text: The three-tier short-term rural cooperative credit structure consists of:
options: Commercial banks, NBFCs and microfinance institutions
PACS, District Central Cooperative Banks and State Cooperative Banks
Panchayat, block and district offices of the government
SBI, RBI and NABARD at the national, state and local levels

questions.question_text: Regional Rural Banks (RRBs) were set up in:
Small Finance Banks mainly aim to provide:
options: Basic banking and credit to small units, farmers and the unserved
Regulation of the other banks in the banking system
Foreign exchange services to the importers and the exporters
The currency notes to the public through the bank branches

questions.question_text: Payments banks in India can:
options: Accept deposits up to a limit but cannot give loans
Give large loans to the corporates against securities
Issue currency notes in place of the RBI
Regulate the other banks and the NBFCs

questions.question_text: NBFCs differ from banks because they:
options: Can accept demand deposits like the savings accounts
Are regulated by SEBI alone and not by the RBI
Can issue cheques drawn on themselves like the banks
Cannot accept demand deposits and are not part of the payment system

questions.question_text: A floating rate on a home loan is one which:
options: Is always lower than the fixed rate on the same loan
Is linked to a benchmark and changes when the benchmark changes
Is fixed for the whole tenure of the loan at the start
Is always zero for the first five years of the loan

questions.question_text: Home loan interest rates are now linked to an external benchmark such as the:
options: Sensex
Exchange rate of the dollar
Repo rate
Gold price

questions.question_text: The EMI of a loan consists of:
options: Part repayment of the principal and the interest
Interest alone, with the principal paid at the end
The processing fee and the insurance premium
Principal alone, with the interest paid at the end

questions.question_text: In the early years of a home loan EMI, the larger part goes towards:
options: Principal
Insurance
Processing fee
Interest

questions.question_text: A loan of Rs 1,00,000 is repaid in one year with a flat interest of 12%. The total repayable is:
options: Rs 1,12,000 per month

questions.question_text: A secured loan is one that is:
options: Given without any documents
Given only to the poor
Given by the government free of cost
Backed by collateral

questions.question_text: Which of the following is an unsecured loan?
options: Loan against fixed deposit
Home loan
Gold loan
Personal loan

questions.question_text: The interest rate on an unsecured loan is generally:
options: Higher than on a secured loan
Zero
Lower than on a secured loan
Equal to a secured loan

questions.question_text: The "margin" on a loan means:
options: The part of the asset's cost that the borrower funds from his own money
The penalty charged by the bank on late payment
The processing fee charged by the bank at the time of sanction
The rate of interest charged by the bank on the loan

questions.question_text: A car costing Rs 10,00,000 is financed with a 20% margin. The loan amount is:
A moratorium period in an education loan means:
options: The period of the processing
The period after which the loan is cancelled
The period of the highest interest
The period during which the borrower need not pay the EMI

questions.question_text: Which one is not a typical document for a home loan application?
options: Proof of identity
Proof of income
Property papers
A school leaving certificate

questions.question_text: A feature of an overdraft facility is that the account holder:
options: Cannot withdraw any amount beyond the balance of the account
Can withdraw more than the balance up to a sanctioned limit
Is not charged any interest on the amount overdrawn
Is allowed the facility only on a student's savings account

questions.question_text: In a cash credit facility, interest is charged on:
options: The entire sanctioned limit
The collateral value
The amount deposited
The amount actually drawn and outstanding

questions.question_text: A bank guarantee is a promise by the bank to:
options: Pay a third party if its customer fails to meet an obligation
Issue a credit card to a customer with no credit history
Give a long-term loan to its customer at a concessional rate
Open an account for a person who has no proof of address

questions.question_text: Letters of credit are mostly used in:
options: Payment of salaries to the staff by a company every month
Payment of income tax by the assessees every year
International trade, to assure payment to the seller
Local grocery purchases made by households every week

questions.question_text: KYC norms are issued by the:
options: SEBI
RBI
Ministry of Defence
IRDAI

questions.question_text: PMLA stands for:
options: Prevention of Money Laundering Act
Post-Maturity Loan Adjustment
Payment and Money Lending Act
Public Money Lending Authority

questions.question_text: Banks are required to report cash transactions above Rs 10 lakh in an account in a year to the:
options: Stock exchange
Financial Intelligence Unit
Supreme Court
Election Commission

questions.question_text: A PAN must be quoted for a cash deposit in a bank account of more than:
options: Rs 20 lakh in a single day
Rs 10,000 in a single day
Rs 50,000 in a single day
Rs 5 lakh in a single day

questions.question_text: A non-performing asset (NPA) is a loan in which interest or principal is overdue for more than:
options: 180 days
60 days
30 days
90 days

questions.question_text: If a bank's gross NPAs are Rs 5,000 crore on total advances of Rs 1,00,000 crore, the gross NPA ratio is:
Provisioning against NPAs is meant to:
options: Increase the profits shown by the bank
Reduce the deposits held by the bank
Cover the likely losses on bad loans
Increase the loans given by the bank

questions.question_text: Basel norms are international standards on:
options: Stock exchange rules
Trade tariffs
Currency exchange
Capital adequacy of banks

questions.question_text: Capital adequacy ratio is the ratio of a bank's:
options: Profit to its capital
Deposits to its loans
Loans to its deposits
Capital to its risk-weighted assets

questions.question_text: A bank with capital of Rs 12 crore and risk-weighted assets of Rs 100 crore has a CAR of:
Under Basel III, banks must keep a capital conservation buffer:
options: In place of the liquid assets under the SLR
Over and above the minimum capital requirement
Instead of the minimum capital requirement
Only if they are making a loss in the year

questions.question_text: The merger of public sector banks in recent years was aimed at:
options: Reducing the capital held by the banks in the system
Privatising all the public sector banks of the country
Increasing the number of banks in the public sector
Creating stronger banks with a larger scale and lower costs

questions.question_text: The Banking Regulation Act of 1949 gives the RBI powers to:
options: Nationalise the insurance companies
Print the postal stamps
License, regulate and supervise banks
Control the stock exchanges

questions.question_text: Nationalisation of 14 major commercial banks took place in:
The Lead Bank Scheme assigns each district to:
options: The post office, which accepts the deposits in the district
A bank which coordinates the credit plans of the district
The RBI, which runs the district's banking services itself
The state government, which lends in the district itself

questions.question_text: A Banking Correspondent helps a bank by:
options: Issuing the licences to the new banks in the country
Offering basic banking services in remote areas for the bank
Fixing the interest rates on deposits for the bank
Printing the currency notes for the bank's branches

questions.question_text: The positive pay system for high-value cheques requires the issuer to:
options: Inform the bank in advance of the cheque details
Return the cheque after the payment is made
Give a loan to the bank against the cheque issued
Pay extra charges to the bank for each cheque issued

questions.question_text: Under the Cheque Truncation System:
options: The cheque is stopped by the drawer before the clearing
The cheque is physically cut into two before the clearing
The cheque is cancelled by the drawee bank on receipt
The cheque is replaced by its electronic image for clearing

questions.question_text: An account that is not operated for a long time (typically two years) is called:
options: Salary account
Dormant or inoperative account
Joint account
Zero balance account

questions.question_text: A joint account with the mode "either or survivor" means that:
options: The account is closed on the death of one of the holders
Both the holders must sign together for every operation
Either holder can operate it and the survivor gets the balance
Only the first holder can operate it during his lifetime

questions.question_text: A nomination facility in a bank account enables:
options: The bank to pay the deposit to the nominee on the depositor's death
The nominee to operate the account during the depositor's lifetime
The nominee to get a credit card
The nominee to get a loan

questions.question_text: Interest on a savings account is credited:
options: Once in ten years, at the closure of the account
Never, as no interest is paid on savings accounts
Only when the customer withdraws the whole balance
At least quarterly, as per the rules of the bank

questions.question_text: A person deposits Rs 20,000 on the 1st of a month in a savings account at 4% p.a. simple interest. Interest for 3 months is:
options: Rs 800
Rs 20
Rs 200

questions.question_text: TDS is deducted by a bank on the interest from deposits if the interest exceeds the threshold. TDS means:
options: Time Deposit Statement
Total Deposit Scheme
Tax Deducted at Source
Tax Deposited by Seller

questions.question_text: Form 15G or 15H is submitted to the bank to:
options: Open a new savings account without producing any KYC
Avoid TDS when the total income is below the taxable limit
Apply for a loan against the fixed deposit of the person
Apply for a credit card with a higher limit than usual

questions.question_text: Digital lending apps in India should be:
options: Operated by anyone without any permission from the regulator
Allowed to access any data stored in the phone of the borrower
Allowed to charge any rate of interest they wish to charge
Registered with or tied to a regulated entity as per RBI norms

questions.question_text: Under RBI guidelines, penal charges on a loan default:
options: Can be set without any limit by the lender at its wish
Must be equal to the contractual rate of interest
Are not to be capitalised, that is, no interest on them
May be added to the principal and charged interest

questions.question_text: The Deposit Insurance and Credit Guarantee Corporation (DICGC) insures deposits up to:
options: Rs 50,000 per depositor per bank
Rs 5 lakh per depositor per bank
Rs 10 lakh per depositor per bank
Rs 1 lakh per depositor per bank
